title: Flood
description: Use this list to prepare for flash floods (minutes of warning) and river floods (hours to days) before the rain arrives.

items.text: Never drive or walk through floodwater: Turn Around, Don't Drown - 6 inches (15 cm) of moving water can knock you down and about 12 inches (30 cm) can float a car
Know the alerts: a Flash Flood Watch means get ready; a Flash Flood Warning means move to higher ground now
Have two ways to get alerts - phone Wireless Emergency Alerts and a NOAA Weather Radio - and keep them on at night when heavy rain is forecast
Look up your flood risk on the FEMA Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov) and learn if you are below a dam or levee
Plan at least two routes to higher ground that avoid low crossings, dips, and flood-prone bridges
Know where high ground is from home, work, and school - and that canyons, washes, and burn scars can flood with little rain
Keep a go-bag packed and ready - flash flood evacuation can mean leaving within minutes
Keep important documents in a waterproof, portable container you can grab right away
Know the plan if trapped: go to the highest floor, never into a closed attic; go onto the roof only if you must and signal for help
Move vehicles to high ground when significant flooding is forecast
Store drinking water in sealed containers on an upper floor or high shelf - floodwater ruins anything it touches
Buy flood insurance early - standard homeowner's and renter's policies do not cover floods, and NFIP policies usually take 30 days to start
Raise the electrical panel, water heater, and furnace above flood level if you are in a flood zone
Clear gutters and drains, and consider backflow valves and a battery-backup sump pump
Keep sandbags or flood barriers for doorways and low openings if you are in a high-risk area
Photograph or video your home and belongings before flood season for insurance claims
Keep waterproof boots, heavy gloves, and N95 masks for cleanup - floodwater carries sewage, chemicals, and mold
Pick an out-of-area contact and write the number on paper
